Where it began

Jason Holder was born in Barbados on 5 November 1991 and went to The St. Michael School. He reached the West Indies one-day side first, in February 2013 against Australia, and a few days later the Chennai Super Kings signed him at the IPL auction. Within a year and a half he had a Test cap, against New Zealand in June 2014. He made 90 runs in that first match, including a fifty, and took two wickets, the first of them Ross Taylor.

The player

Holder was a right-arm medium-fast bowler who could bat properly, and he played 69 Tests for West Indies between 2014 and 2024. He made 3,073 runs at 29.83 with three hundreds and 14 fifties, and took 162 wickets at 30.40, with eight five-wicket hauls and a best of 6 for 42. He also held 71 catches.

His first Test hundred, in Antigua in April 2015, saved a match against England. His best innings came at Kensington Oval, his home ground, in January 2019: 202 not out from number eight, with a stand of 295 with Shane Dowrich, setting up a win over England by 381 runs, the biggest home victory by runs West Indies had known. The year before, he had taken 33 Test wickets at 12.30 in six matches. When he passed 150 wickets in 2023, he joined Sir Garfield Sobers as only the second West Indian with 2,500 runs and 150 wickets in Tests.

What made him special

He was given the captaincy remarkably early. At 23 he became the youngest man to lead West Indies in one-day cricket, and he took charge of the Test side in 2015, at a time when several senior players were often unavailable. He captained in 37 Tests and stayed steady through lean years, which may say more about him than any scorecard.

His bowling relied on height, accuracy and patience rather than raw pace. That did not stop him being, in January 2019, the top-ranked Test all-rounder, the first West Indian to reach that spot since Sobers in 1974. Batsmen did not always fear him at first sight; they tended to learn by the end of the day.

Away from the middle

Cricket West Indies named him its Test Player of the Year in 2019, and in April 2021 Wisden chose him as one of its Five Cricketers of the Year. He was part of the side that won the T20 World Cup in 2016, and in January 2022 he became the first West Indian to take a hat-trick in a T20 international, finishing with four wickets in four balls against England. He played county cricket for Northamptonshire and, in 2025, captained the Los Angeles Knight Riders. He follows Tottenham Hotspur.

And finally

Four wickets in four balls, a Test double hundred from number eight and a World Cup winner's medal: Holder spent his career quietly doing the things that are supposed to be someone else's job. For a captain, that is about the best habit there is.
